description: Pomo Faux Ruins, also known as Postmodern Faux Ruins, is an architectural and interior design aesthetic that was prevalent between the late 1970s and the 1990s, featuring the inclusion of intentionally fragmented, distressed, or crumbling classical architectural motifs. It subverted the pristine, strict rules of Modernism by utilizing structural decay as an educational and playful storytelling device. Unlike the authentic historical ruins, the past Pomo Faux Ruins are overtly commercial, artificial, progressive, and often ironic.
